title: The fall of the theorem economy
author: David Bessis

metaphors.title: Oceans between lemma and breakthrough
metaphors.paraphrase: An ocean separates a technical lemma from a serious paper, another from a breakthrough, and several more from Fields-level work.

metaphors.title: Surveying new continents
metaphors.paraphrase: AI may let young “intuition-maxxers” survey entire new continents at a pace that mystifies their elders.

metaphors.title: Self-driving levels
metaphors.paraphrase: Autoformalization is no more a full solution than Tesla's Full Self-Driving; proposes a Mathematical Intelligence Scale like self-driving levels.

metaphors.title: Mathlib versus Mathslop
metaphors.paraphrase: Formal math splits into an intelligible layer and an unintelligible one; an autoformalized proof sits as an orphaned 200,000-line blob.

metaphors.title: The theorem economy
metaphors.paraphrase: Theorems are the only currency that puts bread on the table; research mathematicians risk being demonetized.

metaphors.title: The Overhang
metaphors.paraphrase: The latent value of connecting existing results, like unrealized capital gains of past creativity, which LLMs are placed to harvest.

metaphors.title: Honor code and Hardy's curse
metaphors.paraphrase: Prove theorems and shut up; “the first rule of the Intuition Club”; a big conjecture as cryptographic proof of conceptual innovation.

metaphors.title: Product recall
metaphors.paraphrase: Mathematics sold a bogus idea of itself to billions; repositioning the brand may be the largest product recall in memory.

metaphors.title: Radioactive wasteland
metaphors.paraphrase: AI companies will bomb formalization into a wasteland that can never sustain life again (Patrick Massot, quoted).

metaphors.title: Caliper to a gunfight
metaphors.paraphrase: Also: a fox thanking the hens for the henhouse keys, collective seppuku, a “nuclear scenario” for the Riemann hypothesis.

metaphors.title: A closed system like Go
metaphors.paraphrase: Hinton calls math a closed system like Go and chess; if AI “wins,” the only loser left is human thought.

metaphors.title: Blenders and the gym
metaphors.paraphrase: Robots outlift us yet we go to the gym; blenders outchew us yet we don't eat through straws.

metaphors.title: Doesn't compile in the brain
metaphors.paraphrase: Unintelligible proofs are meaningless because they don't compile on the only hardware that can appreciate them.

metaphors.title: Samplers and sequencers
metaphors.paraphrase: AI may do for math what samplers did for music; standing on the shoulders of giant machines.
